title: Solution Sample Preparation and Introduction for MS

blocks.name: introduction
fields: Spray Chamber Type and Cooling Temperature

consumed_by: any future solution-introduction MS TAPP (TIMS, solution ICP-OES, IRMS front ends)
notes: Everything upstream of the mass analyser when the sample arrives as a solution: digestion, chromatographic separation, spiking, and the nebuliser/spray-chamber/desolvation introduction chain. Independent of the analyser, so it composes with quadrupole, sector-field or multi-collector.
extraction: Extracted 2026-08-08 under Rule 6.10 from the three Solution ICP-MS TAPPs. Content taken from Solution Q-ICP-MS where present (most literature-assessed of the three, 5 papers). The naive candidate set was 24 fields — 'present in all three Solution TAPPs and absent from LA-Q/SF-ICP-MS'. Eight of those were absent from LA only because LA uses a different NAME for the same field, not because the concept is solution-specific. Those eight were excluded and are logged as cross-TAPP naming inconsistencies to resolve under Rule 1.
reconciliation:
Reconciled 2026-08-10. Tiers and data types were identical across all three source TAPPs; only descriptions diverged, in 13 of 16 fields. Three were byte-identical and needed no decision; `Isotope Dilution Spike` had been decided on evidence at extraction; the remaining 12 were decided by reading, recorded field by field in Archive/Worksheets (reconciled)/SolutionIntroduction_Reconciliation_Decisions.csv.

Outcome: 5 adopted the Solution MC-ICP-MS variant, 3 adopted Q/SF, 4 were synthesized. MC won often not because its text was longest but because its authors wrote trade-offs, which is the highest-value description content.

Governing distinction: naming an ANALYSER ('prior to MC-ICP-MS analysis') disqualifies text from a module consumed by three TAPPs; naming a PURPOSE ('for isotope-ratio work') does not, being a conditional that is true for any consumer doing that work. Several MC variants carried the module's best content wrapped in analyser-naming and were adopted with the wrapper removed.

Two rows went against the 2-of-3 majority. `Nebulizer Type`: SF and MC both said the nebulizer affects 'uptake rate', which collides with the adjacent `Sample Uptake Rate` field; Q's 'sample introduction efficiency' was adopted on the boundary criterion. `Digestion Vessel Type` went the other way, adopting the SF/MC pair for its concrete consequence clause.

The earlier finding stands and is why this was done by reading: the Rule 6.10 criteria are sound as criteria but are NOT automatable by keyword matching. Only the disqualifiers automate.
decisions: Column I (Keyed By) added to every field 2026-08-11 under Rule 7; owned_columns gained "I". Module-owned, so the value is authoritative for all consumers. Also 2026-08-11: descriptions gained an explicit 'Record N/A where...' condition under Rule 7 A.4, propagated to all consumers by recomposition.
2026-08-11: Keyed By revised under the strengthened Rule 7 invariants — every key in use must have exactly one 'defines:' field, and 'defines: X' is used only where another field is keyed by X.
2026-08-12: Keyed By updated for the session/sample restructure (Decision Record A1, A3, A4)

2026-08-14: source_comment declared. Rule 6.11 originally withheld the label from the general modules as noise; with 12 modules supplying most of the library, naming the source of every field is what makes a composed TAPP readable. Documentation only — no structural meaning, not schema content.

2026-08-25: Step 1 of the Description/Purpose split. Column B keeps the Description sentences; the Purpose sentences moved to consumer-owned Column J. Move only — no text reworded or deleted. Routing and rules in analysis/Step1_Routing_ALL_MODULES_2026-08-25.csv.

2026-08-25: Column J `Purpose` declared as an OVERLAY column, not an owned one. The module supplies a default Purpose that a consumer inherits on composition and owns thereafter — the same relationship Column F already has. Added after Step 1 stripped Purpose sentences from Module_ArAr's descriptions with nowhere to put them, because ArAr is composed into no TAPP: a module with no consumer had no destination for its own Purpose text, so the text was lost. Modules now hold it themselves.
tier_provenance: Tier values (Columns C and D) in this module are the library's current best answer and are PROVISIONAL: how hard a field should be pushed at procedure registration and at analysis time is a governance question for community review, not a technical one settled here. They are module-owned so that a review decision lands in one place and reaches every consumer on recomposition — not because the values are considered final.
